clue.text: Whip chestnut Arab’s flanks on week in Scotland …

indicators.note: the flanks of something are its two sides, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: CH is the dictionary abbreviation for a chestnut horse
first and last letters of the word
Scots word for a week

explanation.surface: Someone in Scotland whips a chestnut Arab horse across its sides for a week.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 6 across, where 'there' means Scotland. CHABOUK is a horsewhip, a word from Persian and Hindi.
explanation.definitionFit: A chabouk is a long horsewhip used in the East, so it is a straightforward synonym for a lash.

clue.text: Company’s given lieutenant rope’s end for punishment at sea

definitions.text: rope’s end for punishment at sea

blocks.note: CO is the standard abbreviation for company
LT is the military abbreviation for lieutenant

explanation.surface: A naval officer's company hands a lieutenant the rope to flog a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rope's end' sounds like a fragment to select from, but it is part of the definition: a knotted rope once used to beat sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Colt was the old naval name for a short knotted rope used to flog seamen, hence a rope's end.

clue.text: Cattle disease’s two early elements — getting hot first

indicators.note: the letter standing for heat is taken from the end and placed at the front, rotating the word

blocks.note: two of the four classical elements of ancient philosophy

explanation.surface: A cattle disease is described in terms of ancient elements and fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early elements' are the classical four of ancient philosophy, not the chemical elements a scientist would think of first. H is the usual abbreviation for hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartwater is a tick-borne disease of cattle, sheep and goats in Africa, named for fluid round the heart.

clue.text: NY political society skinned magistrate

indicators.note: removing the skin strips off the outside, so both outer letters go

blocks.note: Tammany Hall, the New York Democratic political machine

explanation.surface: A New York political society has stripped a magistrate of his power.
explanation.walkthrough: Tammany was the notorious nineteenth-century Democratic society in New York; drop its first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An amman is a district magistrate or bailiff in Switzerland and Germany, a variant of ammann.

clue.text: Dipper ducking head to rummage on lake

indicators.note: to duck the head is to lower it out of sight, so the first letter disappears

blocks.note: TOUZE, a dialect verb to tousle or rummage, without its first letter
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A dipping bird dives headfirst to forage on a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dipper' looks like a ladle or a bather, but it is the bird; ducking its head is exactly what a dipper does, which makes the surface vivid.
explanation.definitionFit: The dipper is also called the water ouzel, a small bird that walks underwater along stream beds.

clue.text: Almost erase menu after hacking network ID

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word stops one letter short
something hacked has been cut about and broken into, so the letters come out jumbled

blocks.note: the verb with its final letter dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A hacker nearly wipes a computer menu after breaking into a network account.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing surface is apt, since hacking a network is where an ID matters; the anagram turns ERAS plus MENU into the login name.
explanation.definitionFit: A username is the identifier a person types to log on to a computer network or online account.

clue.text: … stud also covers estates there

indicators.note: to cover something is to have it inside, so the letters lie within the phrase

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Continuing 1 across, the Scottish stud farm also takes in landed estates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'There' refers back across the ellipsis to 'in Scotland' in 1 across. Udal land is held under old Norse freehold in Orkney and Shetland.
explanation.definitionFit: Udals are freehold estates held by udal tenure, the Norse system surviving in Orkney and Shetland, which are Scottish.

clue.text: Routine title of respect given to Rishi

blocks.note: U is the Burmese honorific placed before a man's name, as in U Thant
a rishi is a Hindu holy sage or seer

explanation.surface: A routine honorific is bestowed on Rishi, read as a politician's first name.
explanation.walkthrough: Rishi looks like Rishi Sunak, the former British prime minister, but it is the Sanskrit word for a sage.
explanation.definitionFit: Usage means habitual practice or customary procedure, so it matches routine as a noun synonym.

clue.text: Female entertainers cease to practise around English square

indicators.note: to go around something is to enclose it, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: to give up using something
E is the abbreviation for English
S is a dictionary abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: Performing women give up rehearsing in an English town square.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cease to practise' is one verb, meaning to stop using something. S for square is a dictionary abbreviation rather than an everyday one.
explanation.definitionFit: A diseuse is a woman who performs dramatic monologues or recitations, a French loan for a female entertainer.

clue.text: Flour whitener once a determinant of characteristics

blocks.note: taken as written
the unit of heredity on a chromosome that fixes inherited traits

explanation.surface: A flour bleach was once thought to shape the qualities of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' belongs to the definition: the bleach was banned in the 1950s, so the term is historical.
explanation.definitionFit: Agene, nitrogen trichloride, was formerly used to bleach and age flour until found harmful to dogs.

clue.text: Mugger that’s arrested perhaps writing banner headline?

indicators.note: one who is arrested is held, so this word holds another piece inside it

blocks.note: slang for one of a gang who rush through a crowd robbing as they go
R stands for writing, one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline reports a mugger being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steaming' is British slang for gang robbery by rushing through a crowd, so a steamer is a mugger. The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: In journalism a streamer is a headline running across the full width of a page, also called a banner.

clue.text: Myopia’s zero benefits in force

indicators.note: being in something means being placed within it, so these letters go inside

blocks.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O
benefits as a verb: is of use to
might means power or force

explanation.surface: Short sight is said to bring no benefit at all to an armed force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Benefits' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb 'is of use to'. Zero standing for the letter O is a standard convention.
explanation.definitionFit: Mouse-sight is an old word for shortsightedness, likening a near-sighted person to a mouse with weak vision.

clue.text: Start of labour introducing surprise childbirth technique

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

blocks.note: first letter of the word
to amaze is to surprise greatly

explanation.surface: Early labour brings an unexpected birthing method into play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' sounds like part of the definition, given the childbirth surface, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lamaze method is a system of breathing and relaxation exercises for natural birth, named after a French obstetrician.

clue.text: Hearing of father’s walk in some places …

blocks.note: PA is father, with the possessive S
an ear is the faculty of hearing

explanation.surface: A father's hearing is said to fail on walks in certain places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing of father's' reads as father's ear, so the father comes first. 'In some places' flags a regional word, and the ellipsis leads into 14 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasear is Spanish for stroll, borrowed into colloquial American English for a leisurely outing on foot.

clue.text: Rested satisfied having served well curbing rogue cliques out of line

indicators.note: out of line here means with the letter standing for line taken out
a rogue element behaves unpredictably, so these letters break formation
to curb is to hold in check, so one piece restrains another inside it

blocks.note: to ace is to serve an unreturnable ball in tennis
the word without its L, L standing for line

explanation.surface: A tennis player rested content after serving well and keeping rebellious factions in order.
explanation.walkthrough: ACED is split after its A to hold the rearranged letters. L is the usual abbreviation for line.
explanation.definitionFit: To acquiesce is to accept something quietly without protest, so rested satisfied describes it in the past tense.

clue.text: … a long, tiring walk — pater’s struggling

indicators.note: something struggling is twisting and writhing, so the letters are thrown about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing from 12 across, father struggles on a long exhausting hike.
explanation.walkthrough: Pater, Latin for father and old public-school slang for dad, echoes the father of 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Trape is a variant of traipse, a wearisome or aimless trudge on foot, used as a noun here.

clue.text: Previous government’s need to follow rule of law

blocks.note: r is the abbreviation for rule in legal citation
an obsolete word for need or want

explanation.surface: The last administration had to respect the rule of law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previous government' sounds like a past cabinet, but 'previous' marks an obsolete word. 'Rule of law' is a phrase that here simply means the legal abbreviation for a rule.
explanation.definitionFit: Regence is an obsolete form of regency, meaning government or rule exercised by a regent.

clue.text: South African antelope best developed to conserve existence

indicators.note: something developed has changed form, so these letters are rearranged
to conserve is to keep safe inside, so one piece is held within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
Latin for being or existence, used in philosophy

explanation.surface: A South African antelope is best bred to preserve the species.
explanation.walkthrough: The conservation surface hides the mechanics: 'best' reads as an adjective but is just letters to rearrange, and 'existence' is the Latin philosophical term.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsessebe is a fast southern African antelope related to the hartebeest, also called the sassaby.

clue.text: Decapitation from a blade he flourished

indicators.note: to flourish something is to wave it about with a flamboyant twirl, so the letters get thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An executioner brandishes his blade before a beheading.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a clean executioner picture, with the fodder and the definition both in the same scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheadal is a rare noun for the act of cutting off a head, the same as decapitation.

clue.text: Such large tuna entangled with net causing celebration

indicators.note: entangled things are twisted together, so all the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; these are the letters to remove

explanation.surface: Landing a huge tuna in the net is cause for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: the answer and NET, jumbled together, make CELEBRATION, so take NET away from that word and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Albicore is a variant spelling of albacore, a large tuna of warm seas prized for canning.

clue.text: Perennial largely sewn wildly around in confusion recently

indicators.note: largely means for the most part, so the word loses its final letter
acting wildly means without order, so these letters are rearranged
turning around faces the other way, so the following letters run backwards

blocks.note: the word without its last letter
mussy means untidy or in disarray
late means recently, as in 'of late'

explanation.surface: A garden plant has lately been stitched together in a rough and muddled way.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSSY and LATE are read together and the whole string runs backwards to give the second word's ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweet alyssum is a low-growing scented flowering plant of the cabbage family, grown as a perennial in mild climates.

clue.text: Handle awkwardly in supposed evil confusion and abase oneself

indicators.note: being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: a doubtful word in Hamlet, 'the dram of eale', thought to mean evil
to thumb can mean to handle clumsily
printer's pie is type thrown into confusion

explanation.surface: Someone mishandles a moral muddle and ends up grovelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supposed' is there because the reading of 'eale' in Hamlet is a scholarly guess. 'Confusion' looks like an anagram signal but supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat humble pie is an idiom for admitting error and accepting humiliation, which is to abase oneself.

clue.text: Breakdown company covering mug’s old vehicle

indicators.note: a cover goes over and round something, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: the AA, Britain's Automobile Association, rescues broken-down cars
to mug someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: A recovery firm tows away a fool's clapped-out car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' looks like a noun for a fool, but it is the verb to rob. The AA is the main British roadside recovery service.
explanation.definitionFit: An aroba, or araba, is a heavy covered cart or carriage once used in Turkey and the Middle East.

clue.text: Rare sudden rush parking in capital city

indicators.note: placed in means put within, so this letter goes inside

blocks.note: a capital is the seat of government
P is the sign for parking

explanation.surface: Finding a parking space in the capital is a rare rush of luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rare' belongs to the definition, marking an uncommon spelling of spate.
explanation.definitionFit: Speat is a rare form of spate, a sudden flood or torrent, and so a sudden rush.

clue.text: Prayer beads husband held in backing down!

indicators.note: backing means moving in reverse, so the letters run the other way
something held in is enclosed, so this letter goes inside

blocks.note: French à bas, 'down with', used as a cry of protest
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A husband is told to kneel with his rosary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Down!' is the French cry à bas, written as one word in English dictionaries.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabha, or subha, is the Muslim rosary of beads used for counting recitations of the names of God.

clue.text: Spenser’s to fit question marks in final bits of Faerie Queene

indicators.note: the final bits of words are their closing letters, which are kept
to be in is to sit inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: QU is the abbreviation for question
last letters of the two words
M is the abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: Spenser's Faerie Queene ends with query marks about a fitting conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marks' are question marks in the surface but the German currency in the wordplay. Spenser wrote The Faerie Queene, apt for an archaism from him.
explanation.definitionFit: Queme is a Spenserian word meaning to please or suit, so it stands for 'to fit' in his usage.

clue.text: Photo by watery parts of a Greek god

blocks.note: plural of serum, the watery part of blood
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: A photograph shows a coastal scene, as if of a sea god.
explanation.walkthrough: The photo comes first in the clue but last in the answer, as 'by' means next to.
explanation.definitionFit: Serapic is the adjective from Serapis, the Graeco-Egyptian god of the underworld and healing worshipped by Greeks.

clue.text: Sport’s a way of escape

blocks.note: taken as written
a hunting term, also spelt meuse, for a gap in a hedge that a hare runs through

explanation.surface: Sport is offered as a form of escapism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' reads as a noun, but it is the verb meaning to divert or entertain.
explanation.definitionFit: To sport, in its older sense, is to divert or entertain, which is what amusing someone does.

clue.text: Menial workers rejecting Malaysian dish

indicators.note: to reject is to throw back, so the letters are sent the other way

blocks.note: sate is the Malay spelling of satay

explanation.surface: Kitchen hands refuse to make a Malaysian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: SATE is the Malay form of satay, skewered grilled meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The eta were an outcast class in feudal Japan who did tasks considered unclean, such as tanning.

clue.text: Wears away ploughs round edges of outfield

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters, which are kept
going round something encloses it, so one piece sits inside

blocks.note: ere is an old spelling of ear, to plough
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A farmer's ploughing wears away the margins of an outlying field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ploughs' is an archaic sense: to ear, or ere, land is to till it.
explanation.definitionFit: To erode is to wear something away gradually, as water and wind do to soil.

clue.text: Protest having time for judge covered in hard case

indicators.note: having one thing for another means swapping it in, so a letter is replaced

blocks.note: to object is to protest

J is the abbreviation for judge

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard case' suggests a tough court case, but it is a hard shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtect describes insect pupae enclosed in a hard horny casing with the limbs glued to the body.

clue.text: Sweet joke/hoax inspiring cry from Jacob?

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes another inside

a Jacob is a breed of spotted sheep
a hum is a hoax or humbug

explanation.walkthrough: Jacob suggests the patriarch of Genesis, but it is the sheep breed, so the cry is a bleat.
explanation.definitionFit: Baba au rhum is a small yeast cake soaked in rum syrup, a classic French dessert or sweet.

clue.text: Old chemist’s to refine direct from whisky needing money

indicators.note: needing something means lacking it, so that letter is missing

blocks.note: ex means straight from, as in ex works
malt whisky, often just called malt

explanation.walkthrough: Ex works is a trade term for goods sold straight from the factory, so EX means direct from.
explanation.definitionFit: In alchemy, to exalt was to purify or refine a substance, raising it to a higher degree.

clue.text: Sailor sharing sources where wrecks lie?

indicators.note: sharing a space means being inside it with another, so one piece enters the other

blocks.note: seeds are origins or sources
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: A sailor passes on knowledge of shipwreck sites.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a definition by example: wrecks lie on the ocean floor, though much else does too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunken ships come to rest on the ocean floor, so places where wrecks lie are the bottoms of seas.
